preconditions.description: The number of test cases t is an integer between 1 and 100,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(n, int) and isinstance(m, int) and 1 <= n <= 500000 and 0 <= m <= 500000 for n, m in test_cases)
preconditions.description: For each test case, n (vertices) and m (edges) are integers within specified bounds.

preconditions.expression: all(all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and u != v for u, v in edges) for edges in test_cases)
preconditions.description: All edge endpoints are valid vertex indices within the current graph size, and no self-loops exist.

preconditions.expression: all(len(edges) == m for edges in test_cases)
preconditions.description: The number of edges provided matches the declared m for each test case.

preconditions.expression: all(is_connected(n, edges) for n, edges in test_cases)
preconditions.description: Each graph is guaranteed to be connected.

preconditions.expression: all(len(set(tuple(sorted(e)) for e in edges)) == len(edges) for edges in test_cases)
preconditions.description: No multiple edges exist between any pair of vertices.

preconditions.expression: sum(n for n, _ in test_cases) <= 500000 and sum(m for _, m in test_cases) <= 500000
preconditions.description: The sum of n and the sum of m across all test cases do not exceed 500,000.

postconditions.expression: all(output_lines[i] == 'No' or (output_lines[i] == 'Yes' and 1 < int(output_lines[i+1]) < n and len(set(map(int, output_lines[i+2].split()))) == int(output_lines[i+1])) for i, n in enumerate(test_cases))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is either 'No', or 'Yes' followed by a count c where 1 < c < n, and a list of c distinct vertex indices.

postconditions.expression: all((output_lines[i] == 'No' and not exists_valid_set(n, edges)) or (output_lines[i] == 'Yes' and is_valid_theft(n, edges, set(map(int, output_lines[i+2].split())))) for i, (n, edges) in enumerate(test_cases))
postconditions.description: If 'No' is printed, no valid non-empty proper subset of vertices exists that satisfies the degree modulo 3 condition. If 'Yes' is printed, the provided set of vertices is a valid solution.

postconditions.expression: all(is_valid_theft(n, edges, S) for i, (n, edges) in enumerate(test_cases) if output_lines[i] == 'Yes' and (S := set(map(int, output_lines[i+2].split()))))
postconditions.description: For every 'Yes' case, the stolen set S is non-empty, proper (not all vertices), and for every remaining vertex v, its degree in the original graph modulo 3 equals its degree in the graph induced by V \ S modulo 3.
